referenceUse: Comparison and manually observed numeric contours only. No photograph RGB/depth/scene plate is rendered.
camera: Unchanged physical reference camera and native film path. Stair/paving/terrace height datum unchanged.
geometry: Main roof uses a shared nonlinear neck/late-flare profile and steeper upper pitch across all four connected faces, tile courses, timber deck, structural rafters and purlin rows.
Karahafu uses an eight-station smooth profile with a broad crown and lower shoulder tips; its deck, bargeboard, curved ribs, carving and support sockets share that profile.

Common hall frame has an inferred120mm lateral/100mm rear offset; bay axes, actual turned entasis shafts, stone feet, window framing and attached carvings are coupled. All front feet sit at the existing3.5m landing datum.
Two shallow bearing rows replace the excessive deep upper-eave bracket valance; actual structural timber paths remain.
Added closed gable-end loft walls, real king-post/tie/brace paths and framed clerestory girts/mullions. Roof eave extrapolation is now bounded so rafter tails stay seated under the weather edge.
Two deep curved porch trimmers replace four shallow concentric bands; new return horns, taller closed ridge-end sculptures and lifted central medallion supply the source-led roof skyline.

Main roof tiles now follow constant270mm metric lanes. Outer lanes begin at the real hip boundary; they no longer compress every eave lane into the shorter ridge. Closed cover/pan tiles and seated rafter tails retain actual shape/thickness.
Clerestory frame subdivisions are smaller to avoid oversized false window cells. Gable-wall infill maintains positive depth, and a real ridge timber seats the king posts.

The high oblique exposed a window-like grid inconsistent with the source bearing storey. It is replaced with closed timber boards, projecting girts and real interlocking bracket assemblies; roof/bay silhouettes and fixed bearing datums are retained.
limitations: Dimensions and hidden structure are authored single-view hypotheses.
Actual native full/close/oblique/moving views are required; no diagnostic establishes photographic acceptance.
